reason: The sources support 12 multi-sourced claims confirming the structure's geological origin and debunking fringe claims linking it to Atlantis.
story: Deep in the Sahara Desert of Mauritania lies the Richat Structure, a striking 25-mile-wide formation of concentric rings known as the Eye of Africa. Visible from orbit, scientists originally believed this immense circular landmark was formed by a violent meteor impact. However, extensive geological studies proved it is actually a natural dome created by underground magma pushing upward millions of years ago, which later eroded into dramatic ridges and valleys as wind and water carved away alternating layers of hard and soft rock. Because of its distinctive circular shape, fringe theorists frequently claim the site is the lost city of Atlantis described by Plato. Yet, mainstream scholars emphasize that Plato invented Atlantis as a fictional moral fable. Furthermore, archaeological surveys have found zero evidence of an ancient city or canals, and its location deep inside a desert contradicts ancient accounts of an ocean-bound island that sank into the sea.
angle: The famous 'Eye of Africa' in the Sahara was long suspected to be an alien meteor impact crater, but it is actually a massive natural geological dome sculpted by erosion.

claims.claim: The Richat Structure is a circular geological feature located in the Sahara Desert of Mauritania.
It is prominently known as the 'Eye of Africa' due to its resemblance to an eye when viewed from space.
The structure consists of a series of concentric circular rings and ridges.
Scientists initially hypothesized that the structure was formed by a meteor impact.
Geological analysis proved the structure is actually a natural dome created by igneous uplift and erosion.
Differential erosion of varying rock types created high concentric ridges out of resistant rock and valleys out of softer rock.
Fringe theories claim that the Richat Structure is the real-world site of Plato's lost city of Atlantis.
Fringe claims rely on the structure's circular concentric geometry matching Plato's description of Atlantis.
Scholars and classicists view Plato's story of Atlantis as a fictional myth or rhetorical device rather than a real location.
There is no archaeological evidence of a city ever having been built within the Richat Structure.
The Richat Structure shows no evidence of the concentric water canals described in Plato's Atlantis narrative.
The structure's location far inland within a desert contradicts Plato's account of Atlantis being an island that sank into the ocean.

disputed: Fringe claims proposing that the Richat Structure is Atlantis are unsupported by archaeology and geology; the script should attribute this strictly as an unsubstantiated fringe theory.
The early impact crater hypothesis was disproven after tests showed no evidence of shock metamorphism; the script should frame the impact origin as an outdated historical belief.
